report.verdict: A flat nine-month print that hides a softer third quarter: 9M-26 gross gaming revenue (BSI) of DKK 3,841m (~$568m, +0.5% YoY) and net profit of DKK 1,547m (~$229m, +1.5%) look steady, but the derived Q3 standalone shows BSI down 1.4% to DKK 1,255m (~$186m) and net profit down 4.2% to DKK 503m (~$74m) as the Eurojackpot/Lotto jackpot cycle turned against the lottery monopoly. The liberalised Danske Licens Spil unit (Q3 BSI +7.5%, 9M EBIT +24%) and cost take-out are doing the heavy lifting; FY26 guidance (BSI DKK 5.2–5.3bn, net profit DKK 1.95–2.05bn) is held for a third time and the Elite Gaming disposal tidies the portfolio at negligible earnings cost.
summary: **Flat headline, weaker quarter.** 9M-26 BSI DKK 3,841m (~$568m), +0.5% YoY (+DKK 21m); net profit DKK 1,547m (~$229m), +1.5% (+DKK 23m). Our derived Q3 standalone (9M less H1) is BSI DKK 1,255m (~$186m), −1.4% YoY and −9.2% QoQ, and net profit DKK 503m (~$74m), −4.2% YoY — Q2’s rebound (+8.7% BSI / +19% NI) has not carried into Q3, and Q1 was also down (−5.6% / −10%).

**Mix is the whole story.** Lotteries (Danske Lotteri Spil + Klasselotteri) 9M BSI −2.1% to DKK 2,398m (~$355m); liberalised Danske Licens Spil (Oddset sportsbook, online casino, poker, bingo) +6.6% to DKK 1,238m (~$183m); Elite Gaming slots −2.9% to DKK 204m (~$30m). Danske Licens Spil is now 32.2% of group BSI (9M-25: 30.4%).

**The division that drove the quarter was the lottery.** Danske Lotteri Spil Q3 BSI fell 5.9% to DKK 717m (~$106m, −DKK 45m) on fewer Eurojackpot high pools, smaller Lotto pools and a drop in Quick scratch sales in shops; that single line is larger than the entire group decline (−DKK 18m). Danske Licens Spil (+7.5% to DKK 403m, ~$60m) cushioned it.

**Profit growth is cost-driven, not revenue-driven.** 9M EBIT DKK 2,004m (~$296m), +2.2%, margin 52.2% (+90bps) on flat BSI. ‘Other costs incl. D&A’ fell DKK 55m to DKK 902m (~$133m): other external costs −5.6% to DKK 505m (~$75m, marketing cuts), staff −4.5% to DKK 278m (~$41m), D&A −9.9% to DKK 118m (~$17m). Partly offset by state duties +DKK 17m (+3.7%) and direct game-related costs +DKK 13m.

**No consensus to beat — guidance is the benchmark.** Unlisted, no sell-side estimates. 9M BSI equals 73.9% of the DKK 5,200m low end (9M-25 was 74.1% of the FY25 outturn of DKK 5,158m), i.e. tracking the bottom of the range; 9M net profit is 79.3% of the DKK 1,950m low end (9M-25: 75.9% of FY25’s DKK 2,008m), i.e. profit is tracking comfortably.

**Guidance unchanged for the third time.** FY26 BSI DKK 5,200–5,300m (~$769–784m) and net profit DKK 1,950–2,050m (~$288–303m), first set 13 Mar 2026 and reiterated in June, September and now November; explicitly stated before any effect of the conditional Elite Gaming sale. Implied Q4-26: BSI DKK 1,359–1,459m (~$201–216m), +1.6% to +9.0% vs Q4-25’s DKK 1,338m; net profit DKK 403–503m (~$60–74m), −17% to +4% vs Q4-25’s DKK 484m.

**Event/engagement statistics: none disclosed.** The group reports no handle, actives, ARPU or event data. Management does not mention the June–July 2026 World Cup; Danske Licens Spil growth is attributed to online casino and the GG Poker-powered poker platform launched in Feb 2026. Market context (Spillemyndigheden, GDP-adjusted): Danish betting GGR −42.7% in August and +64.6% in September; online casino +12.5% and +17.9%.

**No formal cost-transformation programme.** Management cites ongoing marketing reductions and lower depreciation (FY24 impairments rolled off: D&A DKK 337m in 2024 → DKK 190m in 2025). 9M capex additions DKK 127m (~$19m) vs DKK 139m; average FTE 480 vs 472 (+1.7%) despite staff costs −4.5%.

**Portfolio: Elite Gaming exit (17 Sep 2026).** Agreement to sell the land-based slot operator (c.6,000 machines) to 87KDSL A/S, owner of Dan-Automater Struer and ultimately Erhvervsinvest — the PE fund that sold Danske Spil its 50.1% in 2012. Price undisclosed; approved at an EGM on 16 Sep; conditional on Danish Competition and Consumer Authority (KFST) clearance; effect to be booked on completion. FY25 BSI DKK 279m (~$41m), net profit DKK 10m (~$1.5m); segment assets DKK 72m (~$11m) at 30 Sep. Our pro-forma: removes ~5% of BSI, <1% of EBIT, lifts group EBIT margin ~260bps (FY25 50.1% → 52.7%).

**Capital position: net cash, no leverage.** Cash DKK 1,399m (~$207m) + securities DKK 832m (~$123m) = DKK 2,231m (~$330m), +2.5% YoY; the only interest-bearing liabilities are leases (~DKK 18m at FY25). Equity DKK 1,851m (~$274m), equity ratio 58.8%. Note the Q3 cash level is seasonally inflated ahead of the Q4/Q2 statutory distributions.

**Cash flow: strong conversion, slight working-capital drag.** 9M CFO DKK 1,860m (~$275m), −3.4% YoY, 120% of net profit (9M-25: 126%); investing outflow DKK 180m (~$27m); FCF (CFO−CFI) DKK 1,680m (~$249m) vs DKK 1,704m. Financing outflow DKK 1,141m (~$169m) is statutory lottery-profit distributions and State dividend — there are no buybacks by construction.

**Financial items are MTM noise.** 9M net financial items −DKK 16m (~$2m) vs −DKK 5m: Q1 −25m (unrealised securities losses), Q2 +26m, Q3 −17m on a DKK 832m (~$123m) securities portfolio. Effective tax rate 22.2% (Danish statutory 22%).

**Duty and regulatory drift.** State duties +3.7% to DKK 474m (~$70m), 12.3% of BSI vs 12.0%, mechanically rising as mix shifts toward the 28%-of-GGR-taxed Danske Licens Spil. Spilpakke 1 (broad political agreement, Oct 2025) tightens online-casino/sports marketing, bans revenue-share affiliate payments and adds youth protections; management welcomes it as levelling a field on which it already self-restricts (no whistle-to-whistle TV ads, no stadium live odds, no affiliates).

**Retail footprint is shrinking fast.** Dealers 3,464 at 30 Sep vs 3,622 at 30 Jun and 3,759 a year ago (−4.4% QoQ, −7.8% YoY, −248 YTD from 3,712). Online was 70% of group BSI in 2025 (64% in 2023). Dealer commission −7.8% to DKK 247m (~$37m) is the offsetting benefit; Quick scratch in shops is the casualty.

**Direct cost creep in the liberalised business.** ‘Other game-related costs’ +16.6% to DKK 239m (~$35m) for 9M and +30% YoY in Q3 to DKK 86m (~$13m) — growing 2–4x faster than Danske Licens Spil BSI, consistent with content/platform/poker-network fees. Gross profit from games therefore slipped 0.3% to DKK 2,881m (~$426m) for 9M and 3.8% in Q3.

**Management, governance, disclosure.** CEO Nikolas Lyhne-Knudsen (since Oct 2020) and CFO Søren Skovdal Rasmussen; Chair Lars Krarup. Quarterly report is unaudited, IFRS recognition/measurement, approved 12 Nov 2026. A new subsidiary, Aurora Alea A/S, is consolidated with no revenue and DKK 1m of assets; purpose undisclosed. Owners: Danish State 81%, DIF 9.5%, DGI 9.5% (AR 2025). No earnings call or transcript exists.

**‘Shareholder return’ is the social contribution.** FY25 total contribution DKK 3,148m (~$466m) incl. DKK 1,787m (~$264m) to the udlodningsmidler (sport, culture, associations). 9M-26 lottery + Klasselotteri EBIT of DKK 1,763m (~$261m) underpins a similar 2026 distribution; the figure is not disclosed quarterly.

**Thesis read-through for the sector.** Danske Spil is a clean read on (i) Danish regulated online casino demand, still growing double digits at market level; (ii) the lottery jackpot cycle, where a strong 2025 Eurojackpot/holiday-product comp (holiday products +24% in 2025) makes Q4 the swing quarter; and (iii) the regulatory tightening coming with Spilpakke 1. The incumbent’s casino-led +7.5% against a +12–18% online-casino market says international operators are still taking share; that window narrows once marketing rules bite.

segments.name: Danske Lotteri Spil (lotteries & scratch — statutory monopoly)
segments.headline: Q3 BSI −5.9% to DKK 717m (~$106m) as the jackpot cycle turned; 9M EBIT held flat at DKK 1,617m (~$239m) on cost take-out, margin 73.7% (+130bps).
narrative: They remain the sole licensed provider of number games and scratch cards in Denmark (Lotto, Eurojackpot, Vikinglotto, Keno, Quick, Alt eller Intet, Klub Lotto and the Plus subscription products), so market share within the lottery vertical is effectively 100% and the competitive question is share of wallet against liberalised casino and betting rather than against other lotteries. Nine-month BSI fell 2.1% to DKK 2,193m (~$324m) from DKK 2,239m, and the quarterly path was volatile: Q1 −10.1% (DKK 659m vs 733m), Q2 +9.8% (DKK 817m vs 744m) and Q3 −5.9% (DKK 717m, ~$106m, vs DKK 762m), with Q3 down 12.2% on Q2. Management attributes the nine-month decline to fewer Eurojackpot high pools, smaller Lotto pools and a drop in Quick sales in shops, only partly offset by Vikinglotto. The H1 report had flagged Eurojackpot ahead year-on-year, helped by a record May draw (358,000 tickets for a DKK 750m, ~$111m, maximum pool, per H1 press coverage), so the nine-month reversal implies a Q3 jackpot cycle that compared poorly with a strong Q3-25, when the segment’s 9M-25 BSI had been running +3.0% on Eurojackpot and Quick.

Profitability held up better than revenue. Nine-month EBIT was DKK 1,617m (~$239m) against DKK 1,621m (−0.2%), a 73.7% margin, up 130bps, on BSI that was 2.1% lower — i.e. the cost base absorbed the shortfall. Q3 EBIT was DKK 534m (~$79m), −3.8% YoY and −13.3% QoQ, at a 74.5% margin (+170bps YoY, −90bps QoQ). The levers are group-wide rather than segment-specific: dealer commission fell 7.8% to DKK 247m (~$37m) as sales migrate online, marketing was cut, and depreciation is lower. The segment generated 80.7% of group EBIT in the nine months (82.7% a year ago), which is the structural point about this company — almost nine-tenths of profit comes from the two lottery monopolies and is distributed by statute to sport, culture and associations (DKK 1,644m, ~$243m, contributed from this segment in 2025 after DKK 20m to Greenland and equity reserves).

Volume, price and luck cannot be decomposed from the disclosure. There is no handle or payout-ratio reporting for the lotteries; BSI is a function of ticket sales and the jackpot roll cycle, and the sensitivity is well documented in the annual report: 2025 had only four Eurojackpot draws at the DKK 750m cap versus 13 in 2024 and 18 high-pool draws versus 27, which cost roughly 2% of segment BSI for the year, and the nine-month commentary indicates fewer still in 2026. Offsetting that, the holiday portfolio (Det Store Jule Lotto, Det Store Påske Lotto, Quick’s Christmas scratch calendar) grew 24% in 2025 — a demanding Q4 comparison — and subscription-type products keep building an annuity base: Lotto PLUS exceeded 210,000 subscribers, Spil Sammen moved onto subscription, and the free Klub Lotto launched in October 2025 passed 100,000 members within months. Twenty-four new online Quick games were launched in 2025 and a further roughly 1,400 new number-game terminals are being installed in 2026 (segment capex additions DKK 51m, ~$8m, in 9M-26 vs DKK 73m).

The retail channel is the structural drag. Group dealer count fell to 3,464 at 30 September from 3,622 at 30 June and 3,759 a year earlier (−4.4% QoQ, −7.8% YoY, −248 since year-end), and the Quick shop-sales decline management cites is the visible symptom; online already accounted for 70% of group BSI in 2025 (64% in 2023, 67% in 2024). Lower commission is a mechanical margin benefit, but Quick and terminal-based number games are the products most exposed to footprint attrition, and the new terminal roll-out is as much defensive as growth capex. Segment assets stood at DKK 1,134m (~$168m) versus DKK 1,362m, reflecting the timing of distributions.

There is no segment guidance. Group guidance implies Q4-26 BSI of DKK 1,359–1,459m (~$201–216m), and with Q4-25 lottery BSI at roughly DKK 772m (~$114m, derived) the lottery needs only a low-single-digit increase to reach the bottom of the range — achievable with normal holiday-product seasonality, but exposed to a weak Eurojackpot roll cycle against last year’s record Jule Lotto and Quick Christmas sales. We would treat the segment as a stable ~DKK 3.0bn (~$444m) BSI, ~73–74% EBIT-margin annuity whose quarterly noise is almost entirely jackpot luck, with retail attrition the slow-burn risk.

segments.name: Danske Licens Spil (Oddset sportsbook, Danske Spil Casino, Tivoli Casino, poker, bingo — liberalised market)
segments.headline: Q3 BSI +7.5% to DKK 403m (~$60m), 9M +6.6% to DKK 1,238m (~$183m); 9M EBIT +24% to DKK 230m (~$34m), margin 18.6% (+270bps) — growing, but slower than the Danish online-casino market.
narrative: They continue to describe themselves as the market leader in Danish sports betting and online casino, while conceding in the 2025 annual report that market share and revenue were under pressure, above all in sports betting, from large international operators with bigger investment budgets. The company publishes no share data, so we triangulate from the regulator: Spillemyndigheden put 2025 online casino GGR at DKK 4,309m (~$637m, +12.1%) and betting at roughly DKK 2.2bn (~$325m, flat), against which Danske Licens Spil’s FY25 BSI of DKK 1,584m (~$234m) equates to roughly 24% of the combined liberalised online verticals, down from roughly 27% in 2024 on our arithmetic. Those are estimates, not company figures, but the direction — a gradual loss of share in a growing market — is consistent with management’s own language.

The nine-month numbers are the best in several years for this unit. BSI rose 6.6% to DKK 1,238m (~$183m) from DKK 1,161m, with the quarterly cadence accelerating from +3.5% in Q1 (DKK 410m vs 396m) to +9.0% in Q2 (DKK 425m vs 390m) and +7.5% in Q3 (DKK 403m, ~$60m, vs DKK 375m); the 5.2% QoQ decline is normal summer seasonality. Management attributes the growth to online casino and to the new poker platform, built on GG Poker’s software and network and launched in February 2026, which gives Danish players access to the world’s largest poker liquidity pool and WSOP qualification. Notably, the June–July World Cup is not mentioned at all; given the group’s self-imposed restrictions on sports marketing (no whistle-to-whistle TV advertising, no live odds on stadium LED boards, no affiliate marketing, deliberately low bonuses), that silence is plausible rather than evasive. Against a regulated online-casino market that grew 17.9% in September, 12.5% in August and more than 20% in July (GDP-adjusted), and a betting market that swung from −42.7% in August to +64.6% in September, a +7.5% quarter implies continued, if slower, share erosion.

The economics that a sportsbook analyst would normally dissect are simply not disclosed: no handle, no net or structural sports margin, no promotional spend as a percentage of handle, no monthly actives, no ARPU, no sports-versus-casino split and no marketing spend in kroner. What can be read from the group P&L is the cost structure of the mix shift. Danske Licens Spil bears the 28%-of-GGR Danish duty (FY25 duties DKK 451m on DKK 1,584m BSI), so group duties rose 3.7% to DKK 474m (~$70m) and their share of BSI climbed to 12.3% from 12.0% as this unit grew while the near-duty-free lottery shrank. More concerning is ‘other game-related costs’, up 16.6% to DKK 239m (~$35m) for the nine months and up 30% YoY in Q3 to DKK 86m (~$13m) — two to four times the unit’s revenue growth, which points to content, platform and poker-network revenue shares scaling with casino and poker volumes. Even so, EBIT rose 24.3% to DKK 230m (~$34m) for the nine months at an 18.6% margin (+270bps on 15.9%), and Q3 EBIT was DKK 73m (~$11m), +10.6%, at 18.1% (+50bps YoY, −50bps QoQ) — operating leverage from reduced marketing and lower depreciation rather than from gross-margin expansion. For context, the full-year 2025 margin was 15.6% and net profit DKK 171m.

On product, the unit spent 2025 rebuilding its digital estate: a new web platform for Danske Spil Casino early in the year, a Casino app (launched May 2024) extended with personalised messaging and improved login, a wave of new titles including the in-house ‘Danmarks Vikinger III’ that reached the top of the game hierarchy, growth at the Tivoli Casino brand under a new brand platform and the Tivoli Casino+ loyalty scheme, a record DKK 707k bingo jackpot in October 2025, and in sportsbook a wider bet-builder and player-props offer via a new international supplier, in-house Danish odds compilation on domestic leagues, and the consolidation of horse racing into Oddset after Dantoto closed in December 2025. On responsibility, the group reports the share of highest-concern players down 69% versus 2021 to 0.24% of casino and sports customers, with AI monitoring and low deposit limits — a deliberate commercial handicap that management says depresses BSI. Segment assets were DKK 1,060m (~$157m) versus DKK 1,097m; nine-month capex additions DKK 39m (~$6m) versus DKK 32m.

There is no segment guidance, and the fourth quarter is the toughest comparison of the year: Q4-25 BSI was roughly DKK 423m (~$63m, derived), the strongest quarter of 2025, helped by the football season and Christmas casino activity. The regulatory backdrop is the other variable. Spilpakke 1, the broad political agreement of October 2025, will curb aggressive online-casino and sports-betting marketing, prohibit revenue-share affiliate compensation and tighten youth protection, with implementation expected in 2027 according to industry coverage; management frames it as levelling a playing field on which it already competes with one hand tied, and a less promotional market would mechanically favour the incumbent brand. Our working assumption is mid-single-digit BSI growth into Q4 (roughly DKK 440–450m, ~$65–67m, our estimate), a full-year margin around 18%, and continued slow share loss in casino until the marketing rules bite.

Management frames it as levelling a playing field; a less promotional market would mechanically favour the incumbent brand.

segments.name: Det Danske Klasselotteri (class lottery)
segments.headline: 9M BSI −2.4% to DKK 205m (~$30m) on fewer players, but EBIT +6.6% to DKK 146m (~$22m) at a 71.2% margin (+600bps).
narrative: They run one of the world’s oldest lotteries, integrated into the group in 2022 and operated as a subscription-based class lottery with monthly draws. Nine-month BSI slipped 2.4% to DKK 205m (~$30m) from DKK 210m, and Q3 was DKK 67m (~$10m), −2.9% YoY and −4.3% QoQ; management attributes the softness to a lower number of players, and in Q1 also to a higher payout ratio. This is the unit lapping an exceptional 2025, when BSI grew 11% to DKK 283m (~$42m) on the ‘15 million-kroner prizes on the 15th of every month’ format introduced in late 2024 — the format change pulled growth forward and the player base has since plateaued.

Earnings nonetheless improved. Nine-month EBIT rose 6.6% to DKK 146m (~$22m) from DKK 137m, lifting the margin to 71.2% from 65.2%, and Q3 EBIT was DKK 48m (~$7m), +4.3% YoY, at 71.6% (+490bps YoY). With a payout-driven cost base and minimal duties (DKK 41m in FY25 on DKK 284m BSI) the lottery converts BSI to profit at a lottery-monopoly rate, and all of that profit flows to the udlodningsmidler (DKK 143m in 2025, up from DKK 130m).

The modernisation agenda is about retention rather than acquisition: card-payment subscriptions were introduced in 2025, MobilePay and Apple Pay are due in 2026, and the ‘Min Side’ self-service portal lets customers manage subscriptions, view tickets and follow draws. Fifty players became millionaires through the lottery in 2025, and the winner stories remain the core of its marketing. Customer numbers are not disclosed quarterly, which is the metric that matters here.

Segment assets were DKK 392m (~$58m) versus DKK 377m, with negligible capex (DKK 2m, ~$0.3m, in the nine months). There is no segment guidance; we would model a flat-to-slightly-down BSI of roughly DKK 275–280m (~$41m) for 2026 and a margin around 70%, with the player-count trend the only variable worth watching.

segments.name: Elite Gaming (land-based gaming machines — conditional disposal announced 17 Sep 2026)
segments.headline: 9M BSI −2.9% to DKK 204m (~$30m), EBIT DKK 9m (~$1m); being sold to 87KDSL/Dan-Automater (Erhvervsinvest) for an undisclosed price, pending KFST approval.
narrative: They operate roughly 6,000 slot machines in gaming halls, restaurants and kiosks across Denmark and describe the company as the largest in its segment, with 24–31 employees based in Tilst near Aarhus. Nine-month BSI fell 2.9% to DKK 204m (~$30m) from DKK 210m; Q3 was DKK 67m (~$10m), flat YoY and −4.3% QoQ. The market is in gentle structural decline — Spillemyndigheden’s September data showed machine GGR down 1% — and the group has been retiring classic analogue units (down about 10% in 2025) while holding the digital fleet flat.

Profit is thin by construction: the unit paid DKK 120m of state duties and DKK 94m of venue commission on DKK 279m of BSI in 2025, leaving a net profit of DKK 10m (~$1.5m) after a DKK 20m goodwill impairment; the parent also wrote down its investment in the subsidiary. Nine-month EBIT was DKK 9m (~$1m) against DKK 8m, a 4.4% margin, and Q3 EBIT DKK 4m against DKK 2m. Segment assets were DKK 72m (~$11m) versus DKK 94m, with capex additions of DKK 2m.

On 17 September 2026 the group announced an agreement to sell 100% of Elite Gaming to 87KDSL A/S, which already owns Dan-Automater Struer A/S and is ultimately controlled by the private-equity fund Erhvervsinvest — the same fund that sold Danske Spil its 50.1% of Elite Gaming in 2012. The deal was approved at an extraordinary general meeting on 16 September, the price was not disclosed, and completion is conditional on clearance by the Danish Competition and Consumer Authority, which opened a market consultation the same day. The CEO described the business as healthy but with limited strategic coherence with the rest of the group; the buyer’s rationale is scale economics in a shrinking machine market. The financial effect will be recognised on completion and the FY26 guidance explicitly excludes it.

The transaction matters more for optics than for earnings. On FY25 numbers it removes about 5.4% of group BSI and 0.4% of group EBIT, and on our arithmetic lifts the group EBIT margin by roughly 260bps (from 50.1% to 52.7%) and the online share of BSI by several points. What to watch is the completion date (Q4-26 or Q1-27), whether a gain or loss is booked against the DKK 72m of segment assets, whether the unit is presented as a discontinued operation, and whether management restates the guidance basis — none of which changes the investment picture, but all of which affect reported Q4 comparability.

highlights.text: Danske Licens Spil is compounding again: Q3 BSI +7.5% to DKK 403m (~$60m), 9M +6.6% to DKK 1,238m (~$183m), 9M EBIT +24% to DKK 230m (~$34m) with the margin up 270bps to 18.6% — online casino and the Feb-2026 GG Poker platform are working, and operating leverage from lower marketing/D&A is real.

Cost discipline is delivering margin on flat revenue: 9M EBIT +2.2% to DKK 2,004m (~$296m) and margin +90bps to 52.2% while BSI grew 0.5%; ‘other costs incl. D&A’ fell DKK 55m (−5.7%) to DKK 902m (~$133m) with staff costs down 4.5% despite eight more FTEs.

Lottery margin resilience: Danske Lotteri Spil 9M EBIT DKK 1,617m (~$239m) was flat (−0.2%) on BSI −2.1%, margin 73.7% (+130bps), as dealer commission (−7.8% to DKK 247m, ~$37m) shrinks with the online mix (70% of BSI in 2025).
Klasselotteri converted a 2.4% BSI decline into +6.6% EBIT (DKK 146m, ~$22m; margin 71.2%, +600bps) — a reminder that the class-lottery annuity is almost all drop-through.

Portfolio simplification: the Elite Gaming sale (undisclosed price; EGM-approved 16 Sep; KFST pending) removes ~5% of BSI but <1% of EBIT and is ~260bps accretive to group EBIT margin on FY25 numbers (our calc.), while exiting a structurally declining land-based machine market.

Balance sheet needs no interpretation: cash + securities DKK 2,231m (~$330m), zero bank debt, 9M CFO DKK 1,860m (~$275m) = 120% of net profit, FCF DKK 1,680m (~$249m), DKK 1,141m (~$169m) already distributed to the State and sport/culture funds.

Guidance held for the third time with profit tracking comfortably: 9M net profit is 79.3% of the DKK 1,950m low end versus 75.9% at the same point of 2025; the implied Q4 range (DKK 403–503m, ~$60–74m) brackets Q4-25’s DKK 484m.

lowlights.text: The 9M headline flatters: derived Q3 BSI fell 1.4% YoY to DKK 1,255m (~$186m) and net profit 4.2% to DKK 503m (~$74m); Q3 net margin 40.1% (−110bps YoY, −300bps QoQ). Two of three quarters in 2026 have now shown YoY declines in both revenue and profit.

Jackpot dependence: Danske Lotteri Spil Q3 BSI −5.9% to DKK 717m (~$106m) on fewer Eurojackpot high pools, smaller Lotto pools and weaker Quick retail — the −DKK 45m swing exceeded the whole group’s decline. Q4 laps record 2025 Jule Lotto and Quick Christmas sales (holiday products +24% in 2025).

Direct cost creep: ‘other game-related costs’ +30% YoY in Q3 to DKK 86m (~$13m) and +16.6% for 9M to DKK 239m (~$35m), growing 2–4x faster than the liberalised unit’s BSI — content/platform/poker-network fees are eating into incremental margin; gross profit from games fell 3.8% in Q3.

Retail attrition is accelerating: dealers 3,464, −158 in the quarter alone, −7.8% YoY and −248 since year-end; Quick scratch and terminal-based number games are the exposed products and the ~1,400-terminal roll-out is defensive capex.

Still losing share in the liberalised verticals: +7.5% against a Danish online-casino market growing 12–18% (and >20% in July) implies international operators continue to take share; our estimate of Danske Licens Spil’s share of online casino + betting is ~24% (FY25) vs ~27% (FY24).

Disclosure is thin for a DKK 5bn operator: no sports/casino split, no handle, net or structural margin, promo intensity, actives, ARPU or marketing spend; no earnings call; Elite Gaming price undisclosed; the purpose of the new Aurora Alea A/S subsidiary is unexplained; quarterly reports are unaudited and give cumulative figures only.

Regulatory and fiscal drift: state duties +3.7% to DKK 474m (~$70m) and rising as a share of BSI (12.3% vs 12.0%) as mix shifts to the 28%-taxed unit; Spilpakke 1 marketing/affiliate/bonus restrictions arrive in 2027 and, while levelling the field, cap the growth ceiling of the only growing division.

forecast.intro: There is no guidance change to bridge: FY26 BSI of DKK 5,200–5,300m (~$769–784m) and net profit of DKK 1,950–2,050m (~$288–303m) were set with the FY25 annual report on 13 March 2026 and have been reiterated in the Q1 (June), H1 (September) and now Q3 (12 November) reports, explicitly before any effect of the conditional Elite Gaming sale. The moving parts are divisional, not group-level: the lottery (Danske Lotteri Spil) is the division pulling BSI toward the bottom of the range (9M −2.1%, Q3 −5.9% on the jackpot cycle), the liberalised Danske Licens Spil is the division pulling it up (9M +6.6%, Q3 +7.5%, EBIT +24%), and cost take-out (other costs incl. D&A −DKK 55m) is what keeps net profit tracking the upper half of its range despite flat revenue. Arithmetically, 9M BSI is 73.9% of the low end (versus 74.1% of the FY25 outturn at the same point last year), so the revenue range requires Q4 BSI of DKK 1,359–1,459m (~$201–216m), +1.6% to +9.0% on Q4-25’s DKK 1,338m, while the profit range requires only DKK 403–503m (~$60–74m), −17% to +4% on Q4-25’s DKK 484m.

forecast.view: Our independent view (all figures estimates): **FY26 BSI of roughly DKK 5,200–5,240m (~$769–775m), i.e. at or marginally below the bottom of guidance**, built from Q4 lottery BSI of ~DKK 785m (+1–2% on a jackpot cycle we assume merely normal against a record holiday-product comp), Danske Licens Spil ~DKK 440–450m (+4–6%, lapping the strongest quarter of 2025 at ~DKK 423m), Klasselotteri ~DKK 72m and Elite Gaming ~DKK 68m if still consolidated. **Net profit of DKK 2,000–2,040m (~$296–302m), in the upper half of the range**, as Q4 duty and direct-cost inflation (duties ~12.5% of BSI, game-related costs +15–20%) is more than covered by lower marketing and D&A; that implies a full-year EBIT margin of ~51–52% (FY25: 50.1%) and a Q4 net profit of ~DKK 455–495m. **Leverage stays nil**: with ~DKK 1.7bn (~$251m) of cash and securities at year-end after Q4 distributions (FY25 year-end: DKK 1,672m), the group remains net cash, and the only balance-sheet event is the Elite Gaming completion, where we would expect a small gain or loss against DKK 72m of segment assets rather than anything material. For 2027 the structural set-up is a lottery annuity (~DKK 3.0bn BSI at ~73% EBIT margin) whose growth is a function of Eurojackpot luck and holiday products, a liberalised unit growing mid-to-high single digits with a sub-20% margin, and a regulatory regime (Spilpakke 1) that should narrow the marketing gap with international competitors; the risks skew to the lottery comp in Q4 and to direct-cost inflation in casino and poker. Note that mix shift toward Danske Licens Spil is structurally dilutive to group margin (18% vs 73%) even as it is the only source of top-line growth.
watch: Q4 lottery jackpot cycle: number of Eurojackpot high/max-pool (DKK 750m) draws and Lotto rollovers versus a record Q4-25 for Det Store Jule Lotto and Quick’s Christmas calendar — the single biggest swing factor for hitting the DKK 5,200m BSI floor.

KFST clearance and completion of the Elite Gaming sale: timing (Q4-26 vs Q1-27), disclosed consideration, gain/loss versus DKK 72m (~$11m) of segment assets, and whether FY26 is restated on a continuing-operations basis.

Danske Licens Spil versus the market: Spillemyndigheden’s October–December online-casino and betting GGR prints (Sep: +17.9% / +64.6%) against the unit’s +7.5% — any widening of the gap signals faster share loss; watch for the sports/casino split in the FY26 annual report (March 2027).
Direct cost trajectory: ‘other game-related costs’ (+30% in Q3) relative to Danske Licens Spil BSI — if the ratio keeps rising, the 18–19% segment margin is at risk once marketing cuts are exhausted.
Spilpakke 1 implementation detail for 2027 (marketing, bonus and affiliate rules, any duty changes) and the group’s ability to re-weight marketing within the new limits.
Retail network: dealer count (3,464, −7.8% YoY) and the ~1,400-terminal roll-out; continued attrition would pressure Quick and terminal number games beyond the commission savings.
Financial items on the DKK 832m securities portfolio (Q1 −25m, Q2 +26m, Q3 −17m) and the FY26 contribution to the udlodningsmidler (FY25: DKK 1,787m, ~$264m) in the March 2027 annual report.
